headline: Compare skipping today with taking today
statement: Given money amounts in a line of houses, choose houses with no adjacent pair and return the maximum total money.
intuition: For each house, either skip it and retain the previous best, or take it and add its money to the best before its neighbor. Only the previous two prefix optima matter.
approach: Initialize two_back and one_back to zero.
For each amount, compute max(one_back, two_back + amount).
Advance the two saved prefix optima.
Return the best for the full street.
correctness: An optimal selection of a prefix either omits its last house, giving the previous-prefix optimum, or contains it, excluding its neighbor and leaving an optimal selection two houses back. The recurrence exhausts both choices. Starting with empty-prefix totals of zero makes the induction valid.
bruteForce: Explore take/skip choices recursively, excluding the next house after a take. Without memoization, overlapping prefixes cause exponential work.

complexity.explanation: Only the two preceding prefix optima are needed.

pitfalls: Do not greedily take the larger neighboring house: choices affect later houses.
